abstracts.abstract: The proliferation of heterogeneous data sources in modern data-driven discovery has exposed fundamental limitations in existing data quality assessment frameworks. This paper introduces a novel theoretical framework, termed Adaptive Data Quality Semantics (ADQS), which reconceptualizes data quality evaluation from static threshold-based metrics to dynamic, context-aware assessment paradigms. Unlike conventional approaches that treat data quality as an absolute property, ADQS formalizes quality as a multi-dimensional utility function influenced by query patterns, analytical objectives, and temporal characteristics of data streams. We derive mathematical properties including monotonicity constraints, compositional quality operators, and optimal quality-cost tradeoffs under resource-limited scenarios. The framework enables rigorous reasoning about quality guarantees in distributed data systems and cloud data management environments. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that ADQS subsumes existing quality models as special cases while providing tighter bounds for data analytics workflows. Experimental validation on synthetic and real-world big data benchmarks confirms theoretical predictions, showing up to 40% improvement in quality prediction accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods. This paradigm shift provides data engineers with principled foundations for designing quality-aware data integration pipelines, fundamentally changing how organizations approach data quality governance in large-scale data processing.

Efficient similarity search in high-dimensional spaces remains a critical challenge in large-scale data processing, particularly for machine learning applications involving embedding-based retrieval. This paper presents a rigorous theoretical analysis of space partitioning strategies that significantly improves upon existingApproximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) search methods. We derive novel theoretical bounds on query complexity and memory-tradeoffs for random-projection-based indexing structures, establishing conditions under which current techniques exhibit suboptimal performance. Building upon these insights, we introduce an optimized partitioning scheme that adaptively adjusts to data distribution characteristics, achieving theoretical guarantees that strictly dominate previous bounds. Our analysis reveals that the proposed method attains query time complexity of O(log N) with sublinear space overhead, representing a substantial improvement over the O(√N) lower bounds previously established for certain parameter regimes. We further prove convergence properties and concentration inequalities for the indexing structure under realistic distributional assumptions. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets with dimensions up to 10,000 demonstrate consistent improvements: 2-3x speedup in query latency with equivalent recall, or alternatively, 15-20% recall improvement at fixed latency. This work provides data mining practitioners with theoretically-grounded guidance for deploying similarity search in production systems.

The emergence of edge computing and Internet of Things applications demands a fundamental reimagining of data management architectures for distributed data systems. This paper presents EdgeChain, a novel system architecture that enables decentralized data analytics at the network edge while maintaining consistency guarantees previously achievable only in centralized cloud data management frameworks. EdgeChain introduces a hierarchical consensus mechanism that orchestrates data flow between edge nodes, regional aggregators, and central cloud infrastructure, effectively bridging the gap between latency-sensitive local processing and globally consistent analytical results. The system incorporates intelligent data routing based on real-time quality-of-service metrics, workload characteristics, and network conditions. We implement EdgeChain as a full-stack solution supporting complex data engineering workflows including stream processing, materialized view maintenance, and ad-hoc analytical queries across heterogeneous data sources. Our prototype handles petabyte-scale workloads across 500+ edge nodes with sub-millisecond query response times for cached results and graceful degradation under intermittent connectivity. The architecture enables new data science applications in smart cities, autonomous systems, and industrial IoT where geographical distribution and latency constraints preclude traditional cloud-centric designs. EdgeChain represents a paradigm shift from centralized to geo-distributed data platforms, establishing new design principles for edge-native data engineering.

Existing approaches to data stream processing in cloud environments suffer from inefficient resource utilization when handling bursty workloads characteristic of big data analytics applications. This paper introduces StreamOptimizer, an enhanced data platform that significantly improves the scalability and resource efficiency of stream processing through novel adaptive scaling mechanisms. The system employs a multi-dimensional auto-scaling controller that jointly optimizes CPU allocation, memory buffering, and network bandwidth provisioning based on learned workload patterns and stream rate dynamics. Unlike prior auto-scaling solutions that focus on single resource dimensions, StreamOptimizer implements holistic resource management through reinforcement learning-guided policy selection, enabling coordinated scaling across the entire processing pipeline. Key technical contributions include a predictive scaling algorithm with provably bounded over-provisioning, a priority-based load shedding strategy that preserves analytical utility, and a failure recovery mechanism with minimal latency impact. We deployed StreamOptimizer on a production cluster processing 10 million events per second from sensor networks and financial trading systems. Evaluation results demonstrate 45% reduction in infrastructure costs while maintaining sub-second processing latency during peak loads, representing substantial improvement over Kubernetes-based auto-scaling baselines. The system seamlessly integrates with existing data engineering tools, providing practical value for organizations managing large-scale data processing in cloud environments.
